newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total says all three French plants on low output.
newsitem.headline: Total says all three French plants on low output.

text.p: A one-day French oil strike has cut output to low levels at the three domestic refineries run by Total, a company spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) La Mede refinery in southern France and 130,000 bpd Mardyck refinery near Dunkirk in the north both joined a stoppage begun earlier in the day at Total's 210,000 bpd Gonfreville plant in Normandy, she said.
"The refineries are running at a minimum level," she said, noting most strikers came from a core group of shift workers.
Union officials said earlier the strikes at Total had been called for one day in sympathy with coordinated 24-hour protests over job cuts at other plants, but they could be renewed.
Near the end of the one-day strike, slowdowns had been reported at six refineries representing 930,000 bpd of production or half French capacity.
A seventh -- Shell's 128,000 bpd plant at Berre near Marseille -- was at a virtual halt in what oil industry association UFIP the day's only serious disruption.
Six refineries were spared any action, according to union and oil company estimates.

France's CFDT union said workers at BP's Lavera refinery, next to Total's La Mede, had threatened to extend disruption from a slowdown to a full stoppage if managers did not discuss the strikes' aims of preserving jobs.
Lavera started running at a minimum viable level on early Tuesday morning, a BP official there said earlier. The strike was scheduled to last one day.
Unions also said a refinery majority-owned by BP at Dunkirk, in which Elf has a share, was also on a one-day slowdown.
The CFDT said action had spread to Trapil, a company operating shared pipelines on behalf of a group of oil firms.
Disruption there included a four-hour closure on Tuesday of the Donges-Metz pipeline crossing France from west to east, a union spokesman said.
The pipeline was once run for military purposes by NATO.
